title: 2026-03-25-quant-kernel-chaos-and-oncall-readiness-lab
summary: Dry-run chaos lab focusing on quantized kernel failure modes, oncall playbook validation, and pre-launch mitigations for next sprint. We exercised fallback paths, verified alerting, and captured gaps in runbooks and telemetry.
topics: Quantized kernel OOM and silent degradation
KV cache evictions and cold-start latency
Oncall escalation paths and runbook clarity
action_items: Marcus: add histogram of KV cache eviction sizes to runtime dashboard (due 2026-04-01)
Diego: prototype a degraded-mode kernel that falls back to fp16 path and run perf baseline (due 2026-04-08)
Aisha: update oncall SLA doc with explicit step for model fallback and service-mesh routing (due 2026-03-30)
Sophie: create 3 regression tests that simulate slow prefix loads for quantized models (due 2026-04-05)
next_steps: Run a second chaos pass next Tuesday with extended traffic patterns (Marcus to orchestrate)
Share adjusted launch gating checklist with Product and Infra by end of week (Lena)
Schedule tabletop with CSM and SRE before dedicated capacity commit
competitors_mentioned: small mention of other inference vendors in market research
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Start: 09:30 AM PT
End: 10:28 AM PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park, Marcus Chen, Aisha Nadeem, Diego Alvarez, Sophie Laurent, platform squad reps

Auto-summary: quick chaos lab to validate fallback paths for quantized kernels and oncall readiness; some telemetry gaps discovered.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Lena Park: okay, uh, thanks everyone for joining on short notice. the goal today is a dry run - run a few failure modes on quantized kernels and see what the oncall playbook actually does, not what it says it does.
[00:22] Marcus Chen: yep, and we'll be doing low-impact traffic, canary lane. we have synthetic traffic hitting the quantized-1 model at 20 qps and a separate cold-start generator.
[00:38] Aisha Nadeem: quick clarification, when you say "quantized-1" that's the 4-bit int path we've been testing right? just want to be sure about the kernel variant.
[00:47] Diego Alvarez: right, it's 4-bit per-token path, with the new reorder kernel. sometimes the reorder kernel is the noisy neighbor when sequence length spikes.
[01:05] Sophie Laurent: one note, our e2e harness sometimes mislabels spikes as parser errors, so expect some false positives in the first 10 minutes.
[01:18] Marcus Chen: go ahead and simulate an OOM on a single GPU, i'll watch the autoscaler and the routing fallback.
[01:27] [sound of keyboard, a brief pause]
[01:42] Diego Alvarez: injecting OOM now... so i force a pager event by allocating a large KV cache for the session.
[01:52] Speaker 2: uh-huh
[02:03] Marcus Chen: we see increased latency at the edge, and the request router starts sending to the fp16 variant after about 18 seconds; the first fallback worked but the instance kept returning 503s for a handful of seconds.
[02:27] Lena Park: is that within our SLA graph or did we spike outside the S-L-A window?
[02:33] Marcus Chen: we temporarily breached the 150ms p95 target for the tenant; p95 hit 210ms during the fallover.
[02:44] Aisha Nadeem: hmm, that means the fallback path isn't warm enough. do we have prefix cache warming in the route?
[02:50] Diego Alvarez: not for the fp16 fallback, no. we rely on auto-prefetch which is too slow.
[03:03] Sophie Laurent: i flagged this in the harness run: cold-start latency from fp16 fallback is around 600ms for the first token on long contexts.
[03:16] Marcus Chen: okay, action: add fp16 warmup after an instance is spun up. but also consider a graceful degrade, like streaming first partial tokens while backend finishes warming.
[03:34] Lena Park: let's keep a note of that. next test, kv cache eviction cascade - diego, you wanted to evict aggressively?
[03:42] Diego Alvarez: yeah, i'll throttle memory to trigger eviction of older KV shards. watch for increased backend CPU as we recompute.
[04:00] [background murmur, brief cross-talk]
[04:14] Marcus Chen: eviction started, saw a burst of CPU on the box. latency oscillated - we had a few timeouts at the batching layer because batch alignment was lost.
[04:29] Aisha Nadeem: that aligns with what we worried about - continuous batching is fragile when we lose KV locality. maybe we need a batch re-alignment window.
[04:40] Diego Alvarez: agreed. naive idea: if U-turn of batch alignment happens, drop long sequences into a separate fast-path queue to avoid blocking shorter requests.
[04:53] Sophie Laurent: question: do we have dashboards showing sequence-length distribution per route in real time?
[05:00] Marcus Chen: we have a coarse histogram but it's not per-route, only global.
[05:07] Lena Park: that's a gap for launch. we need per-route seq-length histograms and heatmaps to catch pathological workloads.
[05:19] Diego Alvarez: also, the kernel selection logic prefers the quantized variant for cost reasons - maybe we need an override based on recent evictions. some signal that forces a temporary pin to fp16 for affected shards.
[05:35] Aisha Nadeem: we should instrument a 'fallback score' metric that combines eviction rate, cold-start latency and cpu pressure.
[05:45] Marcus Chen: noted. i'll add a metric prototype.
[05:53] [pause]
[06:10] Lena Park: let's pivot - simulate a degraded network to a specific AZ and see routing behavior.
[06:21] Marcus Chen: simulating increased packet loss on AZ-west-2b. we should see smart-routing send traffic to the nearest healthy AZ after 30s.
[06:36] Diego Alvarez: in previous runs routing fell over because of our TTL on route health being too long.
[06:45] Marcus Chen: right now it's 60s, which is too slow for customer-facing latency. maybe 15s for this class of failure.
[06:54] Sophie Laurent: but shorter TTL might cause flapping under transient blips, need hysteresis.
[07:03] Aisha Nadeem: put a higher threshold for short inference requests and a longer one for batch background jobs.
[07:13] Marcus Chen: implementing weighted TTL per route class is a decent tradeoff.
[07:21] Lena Park: good, add to runbook: adjust route TTLs and document hysteresis.
[07:29] [simulation continues, ambient typing]
[08:02] Marcus Chen: now i'm going to trigger an alert storm by pushing multiple small failures across nodes to see SRE paging.
[08:14] [phone chime, brief interruption]
[08:30] Oncall Rep (Speaker 4): hello? i got paged, seeing many alerts grouped under kernel-realloc and batch-misalignment. i'm trying to triage, but alert titles are ambiguous.
[08:45] Lena Park: hi - can you describe what your first action is when you see kernel-realloc?
[08:52] Oncall Rep: usually i check the runtime dashboard, then the instance logs for OOMs, then i escalate if multiple AZs are affected, but the runbook just says 'investigate kernel issues' which is vague.
[09:05] Aisha Nadeem: that's the problem. the runbook needs explicit steps: check KV eviction rate, if over X -> pin to fp16, if not -> restart process, if multiple restarts -> traffic shift.
[09:20] Diego Alvarez: also add a quick check to see whether quantized kernel module version changed in the last deploy window - we've seen regressions from kernel swaps.
[09:31] Sophie Laurent: we should keep version info in the alert payload. even an image tag would help.
[09:40] Marcus Chen: agreed. adding image tag and kernel-module hash to the alert context will speed triage.
[09:48] Lena Park: how did the oncall person feel about noise? thoughts?
[09:53] Oncall Rep: the biggest annoyance is tied alerts that don't say which tenant is affected. multi-tenant paging is really noisy. we need better alert grouping and routing.
[10:04] Aisha Nadeem: maybe route tenant-critical alerts to a separate quiet escalation channel for SRE L2 only.
[10:12] Marcus Chen: we'll prototype per-tenant alert policies.
[10:18] [short pause]
[10:30] Lena Park: okay, let's do a second pass on the fallback path - diego, can you force the fallback to happen again but then remove warmup to see worst-case?
[10:40] Diego Alvarez: yes injecting now.
[11:02] Marcus Chen: fallback triggered; this time the router kept trying to send to the spun-up instance for 22s before failing over. we saw queued requests pile up and some 429s.
[11:20] Sophie Laurent: the queue limit is too small relative to spike volume. also, 429 masking makes it look like a client side issue. we need a 503 that indicates server over-capacity.
[11:37] Aisha Nadeem: agreed. also, transparent backpressure would be better than opaque 429s.
[11:45] Lena Park: action: change 429 to a routed 503 with a distinct error code for overload; instrument client libs to retry with jitter.
[11:56] Marcus Chen: note, client retries could worsen overload; the client should back off using exponential with randomized jitter.
[12:06] Diego Alvarez: logging note: some trace IDs are missing when requests hop AZs; correlation breaks across routing fallback.
[12:18] Sophie Laurent: that explains some of the 'ghost' requests in the SLO dashboards.
[12:26] Marcus Chen: fix: ensure trace context is preserved across routing decisions and in the fallback proxy.
[12:36] [mid-meeting check, Lena summarizes briefly]
[12:42] Lena Park: quick recap: gaps found in warmup, per-route seq-length telemetry, alert payloads, and queue sizing/response codes. we've captured a few action items. anything else before we simulate the launch checklist?
[12:55] Diego Alvarez: one more - quantization regressions are tricky; we should add a canary baseline that runs a short eval on each deploy to compare token thinning metrics.
[13:07] Sophie Laurent: yes, regression alert if token distribution deviates beyond threshold.
[13:15] Aisha Nadeem: i'll add a 'smoke-eval' step to the CD pipeline for quantized kernels.
[13:25] [audio: brief laughter]
[13:40] Lena Park: okay last section - tabletop: you are SRE L2 on duty, synthetic ramp hits production lane, what does your runbook say?
[13:51] Oncall Rep: first check the per-route heatmaps -> if single route affected, pin traffic away, if global, trigger incident bridge.
[14:05] Lena Park: do we have an incident bridge playbook mapped to customer impact levels?
[14:12] Marcus Chen: lightly. we have impact levels 1-3 but mapping to customer-visibility needs tightening.
[14:23] Aisha Nadeem: add explicit thresholds: e.g., >5% tenant error rate for 90s => P1 prep, >20% => open bridge.
[14:35] Diego Alvarez: add an automated suppression step for noisy alerts while team does triage, so we don't cascade pages.
[14:45] Sophie Laurent: and ensure CSMs get a sanitized summary so they can message customers early.
[14:53] Lena Park: good. we'll draft communication templates.
[15:03] [noise - someone typing]
[15:20] Marcus Chen: wrapping up the chaos lab - overall the fallback paths work but are slow and noisy; a few concrete telemetry and runbook fixes will dramatically reduce oncall toil.
[15:34] Lena Park: ok final recap and next steps: Marcus will add metrics and per-route histograms; Diego will prototype degraded-mode kernel fallback; Aisha will update runbook with explicit steps and thresholds; Sophie will add regression tests and smoke-eval to the pipeline. we'll reconvene next Tuesday for pass two.
[15:56] Oncall Rep: thanks, appreciate the tabletop - that was helpful.
[16:05] Lena Park: thanks everyone. end of meeting.

--- End transcript ---
